name: Carsten Maschmeyer
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2021-2025); Hurun Global (2023-2026)
forbes_bio: Carsten Maschmeyer founded German financial services provider AWD Holding AG in 1988 and took it public in 2000.
After Swiss Life acquired his AWD stake in 2008, Maschmeyer cofounded a consulting boutique focused on pension and health care plans.
Today, he invests in renewable energy and startups and runs his own asset management company, Paladin.
forbes_facts: He is married to German actress Veronica Ferres and has two sons from his first marriage.

name: Ayhan Tosyali
appears_on: Forbes real-time (former) (2020); Forbes annual (2018-2019); Hurun Global (2020-2022)
forbes_bio: Ayhan Tosyali is vice chairman of steel and iron producer Tosyali Holding, which has 18 facilities spread over Turkey, Serbia and Algeria.
As a child, he joined his father and brothers in a small workshop in Iskenderun, where they made sheet metal out of used tin cheese cans.
From sheet metal, they went on to bucket and stove production. The family began investing in Algeria in 2008.
Including overseas operations, Tosyali is on track to become Turkey's largest iron and steel producer, with an 8.5 million ton capacity by 2019.
Ayhan shares ownership in the business with his brothers Fuat and Fatih Tosyali, who are also billionaires.
forbes_facts: By the end of 2019, Tosyali Holding expects to have invested in excess of $6 billion in integrated production facilities located in Oran, Algeria.

name: Wang Wenjing
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2010-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026); Hurun China (2000-2026)
forbes_bio: China's software industry pioneer Wang Wenjing chairs Yonyou Network Technology, once known as UFIDA.
Wang began his undergraduate studies at age 15 and founded Yonyou at age 24.
Outside of the office, Wang's interests include wine, golf and tennis.

name: Chang Jianming
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2023-2025); Hurun Global (2023-2026); Hurun China (2020-2026)
forbes_bio: Chang Jianming chairs Shanghai Moons, a maker of industrial equipment for the automotive industry.
Moons went public on the Shanghai Stock Exchange in 2017.
The company was founded in Shanghai in 1994 and employs more than 3,000 people.

name: Paritosh Garg
forbes_bio: Paritosh Garg is the chairman of  Happy Forgings, which he founded in the northern Indian city of Ludhiana in 1979.
The company produces parts such as crankshafts and axles for a range of industries from automobiles  to oil and gas to wind energy.
Happy Forgings got listed in December 2023 at an 18% premium to its IPO price.
His son Ashish Garg, an engineering graduate from the University of Warwick, is the company's managing director.

name: Smagulov Nurlan
forbes_bio: Nurlan Smagulov is the founder and president of Astana Group, a Kazahkstani business with interests in car dealerships and shopping malls.

The group was founded in 1992 as Astana Motors, a car dealership, which now operates as a distributor and dealer for over a dozen automobile brands, as well as a manufacturer of passenger and commercial vehicles.
Smagulov launched one of the country's first modern shopping and entertainment center formats, MEGA, in 2006.
In 2025, he built Kazakhstan's first private museum of contemporary art, the Almaty Museum of Arts, investing more than $120 million in the project.
The museum will include works by Richard Serra, Anselm Kiefer, Yayoi Kusama, and Bill Viola, as well as art by Yinka Shonibare, Jaume Plensa, and Alicja Kwade created specifically for the museum.
forbes_facts: Astana Motors Manufacturing produces the Chinese car brands Chery, Changan, Haval, and Tank.

name: Yu Peidi
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2001-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2018); Hurun China (2012-2021)
forbes_bio: Yu Peidi chairs Shanghai-listed real estate developer Greattown Holdings.
Yu left his hometown Fuzhou in 1976 and got his start in the home appliances trade in Indonesia.
Yu began to invest in Fuzhou in the 1980s, starting with minerals and later real estate.

name: Cheng Lili
forbes_bio: Cheng Lili chairs Jiangsu Lihua Animal Husbandry, a chicken breeder and supplier of poultry feed.
Lihua debuted at the Shenzhen Stock Exchange on Feb. 28, 2019, after raising $171 million in an IPO.
Lihua is headquarterd in the eastern Chinese city of Changzhou.

name: Carsten Koerl
sec_insider_companies: Sportradar Group AG (SRAD) - Chief Executive Officer
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2022-2025); Hurun Global (2022-2026); SEC insider holdings (2026); Hurun Unicorn founders (2020)
forbes_bio: Carsten Koerl founded and runs sports data firm Sportradar, which he took public on the Nasdaq in 2021.
Sportradar, based in Switzerland, helps sports leagues compile data like in-game statistics and distribute it to media companies and betting operators.
He made his first entry into the sports data space in 1997 by founding Bwin (then called betandwin), later taking it public on Austria's Vienna Stock Exchange.
He earned a master's degree in electronic and microprocessor engineering from the University for Applied Sciences in Konstanz, Germany.
forbes_facts: Koerl developed a love for sports and competition during his youth and was an avid fan of German soccer club Bayern Munich.
Michael Jordan, Mark Cuban, Washington Capitals owner Ted Leonsis and Los Angeles Dodgers part-owner Todd Boehly all own minority stakes in Sportradar.

name: Sheila Johnson
forbes_bio: Sheila Johnson cofounded cable TV channel Black Entertainment Television in 1979 with her then-husband Robert Johnson. Viacom bought it for $3 billion in 2001.
After her divorce in 2002, she sold her BET shares and has since invested in a portfolio of hotels known as the Salamander Collection, as well as other real estate and horses.
Her Innisbrook resort in Palm Harbor, Florida, hosts an annual PGA Tour championship.
She was an executive producer of the critically-acclaimed 2013 film The Butler, which tells the story of a former slave turned White House employee.
Through her investment in Monumental Sports & Entertainment, she owns stakes in three Washington sports teams: the WNBA's Mystics, NBA's Wizards and NHL's Capitals.
forbes_facts: Johnson is the only black woman to own stakes in three professional sports teams.
Johnson's parents enrolled her in an all-white school in early 1950s Kentucky before desegregation was federally mandated.
